NNMT is an enzyme that transfers a methyl group from S-adenosyl-L-methionine to nicotinamide, forming 1-methylnicotinamide and S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine. Because this pathway intersects nicotinamide metabolism, methyl-donor balance, NAD-related cellular processes, and energy homeostasis, NNMT has become a research target in metabolic biology. Published biochemical and cellular studies have characterized 5-Amino-1MQ as an NNMT-directed inhibitor and experimental probe for examining these pathways.

In cultured adipocyte systems, published experiments have evaluated 5-Amino-1MQ for effects on NNMT activity, intracellular 1-methylnicotinamide, NAD-related measurements, methyl-donor metabolites, and lipogenesis-associated endpoints. Results depend on cell type, assay design, concentration, exposure period, analytical method, and experimental controls.
